scenes.title: INSERT
scenes.narration: INSERT adds new rows to a table, the primary way data enters your database.

scenes.title: Adding rows
bullets: Names the target table and columns
Can insert several rows at once
scenes.narration: INSERT specifies the table and the columns you intend to populate. It then supplies values that line up with those columns in order. A single statement can add many rows, which is efficient for bulk loading.

scenes.title: Inserting rows
scenes.code:
INSERT INTO customers (id, name, created_at)
VALUES
  (1, 'Ana', '2024-05-01'),
  (2, 'Ben', '2024-05-02');
scenes.narration: This statement adds two new customers to the table in one call. The column list defines the order in which values are read. Each row in the VALUES list maps its entries to id, name, and created_at respectively.

scenes.title: How a row is added
scenes.narration: You name the table and the columns you are filling, then provide one value tuple per row. The database validates each value against the column's data type and constraints. Rows that pass are appended to the table.

scenes.text: List columns explicitly in INSERT so your statements stay clear and resilient to schema changes.
scenes.narration: Always name the columns in an INSERT so the mapping stays obvious and the statement keeps working even if the table gains new columns.
